chapters: The words of Nechemiah the son of Chachalyah. And it came to pass in the month of Kislev [in] the twentieth year that I was in Shushan the capital.
There came Chanani, one of my brethren, he and men from Yehudah, and I asked them about the Yehudim who had escaped, who remained of the captivity, and about Yerushalayim.
And they said to me, "The remnant who remained of the captivity in the province are in great trouble and reproach; and the wall of Yerushalayim is breached, and its gates were burned with fire."
And it came to pass when I heard these words that I sat and wept, and I mourned for days, and I fasted and prayed before the Elokim of heaven.
And I said, "I beseech You, O Havayah Elokim of heaven, the great and awesome El, Who keeps the Covenant and loving-kindness to those who love Him and to those who keep His commandments.

Let Your ear now be attentive and Your eyes open to listen to the prayer of Your servant, which I pray before You today, day and night, concerning the Children of Yisroel, Your servants, and I confess the sins of the Children of Yisroel, which we sinned against You; and I and my father's house have sinned.
We have dealt corruptly against You, and we have not kept the commandments, the statutes, and the ordinances that You commanded Moshe, Your servant.
Remember now the word that You commanded Moshe, Your servant, saying, 'If you deal treacherously, I shall scatter you among the nations.

And if you return to Me and keep My commandments and perform them — if your exile is at the end of the heaven, from there I shall gather them, and I shall bring them to the place that I chose to cause My Name to rest there.'
Now they are Your servants and Your people, whom You redeemed with Your great strength and with Your strong hand.

I beseech You, O Master, may Your ear now be attentive to the prayer of Your servant and to the prayer of Your servants, who wish to fear Your name, and cause Your servant to succeed today, and grant him mercy before this man." And I was the king's butler.

Now it came to pass in the month of Nissan, in the twentieth year of King Artachshasta, [that they brought] wine before him, and I carried the wine and gave [it] to the king. And I had never been sad in his presence.
And the king said to me, "Why do you have a sad countenance? You are not ill. This is nothing but wickedness of heart." And I became very frightened.
And I said to the king, "May the king live forever! Why should my countenance not be sad when the city, the place of my forefathers' graves, is laid waste, and its gates are consumed by fire?"
And the king said to me, "For what do you make request?" And I prayed to the Elokim of heaven.
And I said to the king, "If it pleases the king, and if your servant is pleasing before you, that you send me to Yehudah, to the city of the graves of my forefathers, and I shall build it."
And the king said to me — and the queen was sitting beside him-"How long will your trip take, and when will you return?" And it pleased the king, and he sent me, and I gave him a time.
And I said to the king, "If it pleases the king, may letters be given to me to the governors of the land beyond the river, that they escort me through until I come to Yehudah.

And a letter to Asaf, the guardian of the king's orchard, that he give me wood to make beams for the gates of the castle that belongs to the Temple and for the wall of the city and for the house to which I shall go," and the king gave me according to the good hand of my Elokim upon me.
And I came to the governors of the land beyond the river, and I gave them the king's letters, and the king sent with me officers of the army and horsemen.
Now Sanbalat the Horoni and Toviyah the Ammoni slave heard, and it displeased them greatly, that a man had come to request good for the Children of Yisroel.
And I came to Yerushalayim, and I was there for three days.

And I and a few men with me arose at night, and I did not tell anyone what my Elokim had put into my heart to do for Yerushalayim, and there were no animals with me except the animal upon which I was riding.

And I went out through the Gate of the Valley at night and toward En Hattannin and to the Dung Gate, and I was breaking the walls of Yerushalayim, which were breached, and its gates [which were] consumed by fire.
And I passed to the Fountain Gate and to the king's pool, and there was no place for the animal that was under me to pass.
And I ascended by the valley at night, and I broke into the wall, and I returned and came into the gate of the valley, and I returned.
And the prefects did not know where I went and what I was doing, and the Yehudim, the priests, the nobles, the prefects, and the remaining performers of the work I had not yet told.

And I said to them, "You see the sad state we are in, that Yerushalayim is laid waste, and its gates have been burned with fire; come and let us build the wall of Yerushalayim, and we shall no longer be a reproach."

And I told them of the hand of my Elokim, which was good upon me, and also the words of the king that he said to me. And they said, "Let us get up and build," and they strengthened their hands for good.

Then Sanbalat the Horoni, and Toviyah the Ammoni slave, and Geshem the Arvi heard, and they mocked us and despised us, and they said, "What is this thing that your are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"

And I answered them a word, and I said to them, "The Elokim of heaven-He will make us succeed, and we, His servants, will get up and build, but you have no share, charity, or remembrance in Yerushalayim."

Then Eliashib the High Priest and his brothers the priests arose and built the Sheep Gate; they hallowed it and erected its doors, and until the Tower of the Hundred they hallowed it, until the Tower of Hananel.
And next to it the men of Yericho built, and next to it Zaccur the son of Imri built.
And the sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate; they laid its beams and erected its doors, its locks, and its bolts.

And next to them, Meremoth the son of Uriyah, the son of Hakkoz repaired, and next to them Meshullam the son of Berechyah, the son of Meshezabel repaired, and next to them Tzadok the son of Baana repaired.
And next to them, the Tekoim repaired, but their mighty men did not bring their neck into the service of their master.
And Yoyada the son of Paseah and Meshullam the son of Besodyah repaired the gate of the old [city]; they laid its beams and erected its doors, its locks, and its bolts.
And next to them Melatyah the Givoni, and Yadon the Meironosi, [and] the men of Givon and Mitzpah repaired, and next to him a throne for the governor of the land beyond the river.
Next to him Uziel the son of Charayah, [of the] goldsmiths, repaired, and next to him, Chananyah the son of the perfumers repaired, and they filled Yerushalayim until the broad wall.
And next to them, Refayah the son of Hur, the ruler of half the district of Yerushalayim repaired.
And next to them Yedayah the son of Harumaph repaired and [it was] opposite his house, and next to him Hattush the son of Chashavneyah repaired.
Malkijah the son of Harim and Hashub the son of Pahath-Moav repaired a second measure, and [also] the Tower of the Furnaces.
Next to him Shalum the son of Hallohesh, the ruler of half the district of Yerushalayim, he and his daughters repaired.
Chanun and the dwellers of Zanoah repaired the Gate of the Valley; they built it, and they erected its doors, its locks, and its bolts, and a thousand cubits in the wall until the Dung Gate.
Malkijah the son of Rechab, the prince of the district of Beis Hakkerem, repaired the Dung Gate; he built it and erected its doors, its locks, and its bolts.

And Shallun, the son of Kol Hozeh, the ruler of the district of Mitzpah, repaired the Gate of the Fountain; he built it and roofed it and erected its doors, its locks, and its bolts, and the wall of the pool of Shelach toward the king's garden and until the steps descending from the City of Dovid.
After him Nechemiah the son of Azbuk, the ruler of half the district of Beis Zur, repaired until opposite the sepulchers of Dovid and until the [man-]made pool and until the house of the mighty men.
After him the Leviim, Rechum the son of Bani repaired; next to him Chashavyah, the ruler of half the district of Keilah, repaired for his district.
After him their brothers repaired, Bawai the son of Henadad, the ruler of half the district of Keilah.
And Ezer the son of Yeshua, the ruler of Mitzpah, repaired next to him a second measure, opposite the ascent to the armory, at the corner.
After him, Baruch the son of Zaccai repaired a second measure from the corner until the entrance to the house of Eliashib the High Priest.
After him Meremoth the son of Uriyah, the son of Hakkoz repaired a second measure from the entrance of the house of Eliashib until the end of the house of Eliashib.
And after him the priests, the men of the plain, repaired.
And after it, Binyamin and Hishub repaired opposite their house; after him Azaryah the son of Maaseyah, the son of Chananyah repaired next to his house.
After him Binnui the son of Henadad repaired a second measure from the house of Azaryah until the corner and until the tower.
Palal the son of Uzai [built] from opposite the corner and the tower that juts out of the upper house of the king, which is near the prison yard; after him was Pedayah the son of Parosh.
And the Nethinim dwelt in the Ofel until opposite the Water Gate to the east and the tower that juts out.
After him the Tekoim repaired a second measure, from opposite the great tower that juts out until the wall of the Ofel.
Above the Gate of the Horses the priests repaired, each one opposite his house.
After him Tzadok the son of Immer repaired opposite his house, and after him Shemayah the son of Shechanyah, the guardian of the Eastern Gate, repaired.
After him Chananyah the son of Shelemyah and Chanun the sixth son of Zalaph repaired a second measure; after him Meshullam the son of Berechyah repaired opposite his chamber.
After him Malkijah the son of Hatzorefi repaired until the house of the Nethinim and the peddlers, opposite the Hammifkad Gate, and until the ascent to the tower.
And between the ascent to the tower and the Sheep Gate, the smiths and the peddlers repaired.
And it came to pass when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he became wroth and was very angry, and he ridiculed the Yehudim.

And he spoke before his brethren and the army of Shomron, and he said, "What are the feeble Yehudim doing? Will they let them? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in one day? Will they revive the stones from the heaps of dust, for they are burnt?"
And Toviyah the Ammoni was beside him, and he said, "Even what they build, if a fox comes up and breaches the wall of their stones?"
"Hearken, our Elokim, for we have been despised, and return their reproach upon their head and cause them to be despised in a land of captivity.
And do not conceal their iniquity and do not erase their sin from before You, for they have provoked the builders."
But we built the wall, and the entire wall was built to its half, and the people had a desire to build.

Now it came to pass when Sanballat, and Toviyah, and the Arvim, and the Ammonim, and the Ashdodim heard that the wall of Yerushalayim was repaired, that the people who were exposed had commenced to be closed in, that they became very angered.
And they all banded together to come to wage war against Yerushalayim and to wreak destruction therein.
And we prayed to our Elokim, and we stationed a watch over them day and night because of them.
And Yehudah said, "The porter's strength has failed, and there is much earth, and we cannot build the wall."
And our adversaries said, "They will not know and they will not see until we come into their midst, and we shall slay them and stop the work."
Now it came to pass when the Yehudim who dwelt beside them came, that they said to us ten times, "From all the places that you shall return upon us."
So I stationed [mighty men] from below the place, from behind the wall on the bare rocks, and I stationed the people according to families, with their swords, their spears, and their bows.

And I saw, and I arose, and I said to the nobles and to the prefects and to the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them; remember the great and awesome Master, and fight for your brethren, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your households."
And it came to pass when our enemies heard that it had become known to us, that Elokim had frustrated their counsel, that we all returned to the wall, each one to his work.
And it was from that day on, half of my youths did work and half of them held spears, shields, bows, and coats of mail, and the rulers were behind the entire House of Yehudah.
The builders of the wall and the carriers of the loads were loading, with one hand doing the work and one holding the sword.
And the builders, each one with his sword bound to his waist, and [they were] building, and the one who sounded the shofar was beside me.
And I said to the nobles and to the prefects and to the rest of the people, "There is much work, and [it is] widespread, and we are separated on the wall, one far from the other.
In the place that you will hear the sound of the shofar, there you shall gather to us; our Elokim will fight for us."
And we were doing work, and half of them were holding spears from the rise of dawn until the emergence of the stars.
Also at that time I said to the people, "Let each man and his youth lodge in the midst of Yerushalayim, and the night will be for our watch and the day for work."
And I, and my brothers, and my youths, and the men of the watch who followed me — we did not take off our clothes; no man took it even to the water.
Now the cry of the people and their wives was great about their brothers, the Yehudim.
There were some who were saying, "Our sons and our daughters and we, are many; now we shall buy corn and eat and live."
And there were some who were saying, "Our fields and our vineyards and our houses we shall pledge, so that we shall buy corn for the hunger."
And there were some who were saying, "We have borrowed money for the king's tax on our fields and our vineyards.

And now, like the flesh of our brethren is our flesh; like their children are our children, and behold, we are subjecting our sons and daughters to slavery, and some of our daughters are [already] subjected, and we have no power, and others have our fields and vineyards."
And I was very distressed when I heard their cry and these words.
And I thought this over to myself, and I contended with the nobles and with the prefects, and I said to them, "Are you demanding each other's loans?" And I gathered a large assembly around them.

And I said to them, "We bought our Yehudi brethren who were sold to the nations with as much as we could afford, and you too will sell your brethren, and they will be sold to us." And they remained silent and could find no answer.
So I said, "The thing you are doing is not good. Is it not so that you will go with the fear of our Elokim because of the reproach of the nations, our enemies?
I, too, and my brothers, and my servants have lent them money and corn. Let us now relinquish this loan.
As of today, give them back their fields, vineyards, olive trees, and houses, and the hundred silver pieces, and the corn, the wine, and the oil that you lent them."
And they said, "We shall return, and we shall not demand of them; so shall we do as you say." And I called the priests and adjured them to do according to this promise.

I also shook out my garment and said, "So shall Elokim shake out any man who does not fulfill this matter, from his house and from his toil, so shall he be shaken out and empty." Then the entire congregation said, "Amen," and they praised Havayah, and the people did according to this word.

Also, since the day that he commanded me to be a governor in the land of Yehudah, from the twentieth year until the thirty-second year of King Artachshasta, twelve years, my brethren and I have not eaten the food allotted to the governor.

But the early governors who were before me burdened the people and took from them for bread and wine above forty silver shekels. Also, their servants ruled over the people, but I did not do that because of the fear of Elokim.
Also, I adhered to the work of this wall, and we did not buy a field, and all my servants were gathered there over the work.
And the Yehudim and the prefects were one hundred and fifty men, and those who came to us from the nations around us at my table.

And this is what was prepared for one day; one ox, six choice sheep, and birds were prepared for me, and as much as ten days' supply of all types of wine in quantity, and with this, I did not seek the food allotted to the governor, because the work was heavy upon this people.
Remember for me, My Elokim, for good, all that I did for this people."

Now it came to pass, when it was heard by Sanballat, Toviyah, Geshem the Arvi, and the rest of our enemies that I had built the wall, and that no breach was left therein; also that until that time I had not erected doors in the gates.
Then Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, "Come and let us meet together in Kefirim in the Valley of Ono"; and they were plotting to do me harm.
And I sent messengers to them, saying, "I am doing great work, and I cannot go down. Why should the work stop when I leave it and come down to you?"
And they sent to me four times according to this wording, and I answered them according to this wording.
Then Sanballat sent to me according to this wording a fifth time with his servant, and an open letter was in his hand.

It was written in it, "It is heard among the nations, and Gashmu says that you and the Yehudim are plotting to rebel; therefore, you are building the wall, and you are their king." According to these words,

"You have also set up speakers to call upon you in Yerushalayim, saying, 'There is a king in Yehudah,' and now it will be reported to the king according to these words; so let us come and take counsel together."
So I sent to him, saying, "Such as these words that you say never happened; you are inventing them from your heart.
For they all fear us, saying, 'Let their hands be slackened from the work, and let it not be done,' and now, strengthen my hands."

And I came to the house of Shemayah the son of Delayah, the son of Mehetabel, and he was confined, and he said, "Let us meet in the House of Elokim, in the midst of the Temple, and let us close the doors of the Temple, for they are coming to assassinate you; tonight they are coming to assassinate you."
So I said to him, "Will a man like me flee? And who is like me who will enter the Temple and live? I will not enter. "
And I discerned, and behold, Elokim had not sent him, for he spoke prophecy concerning me, and Toviyah and Sanballat had hired him.
For this he was hired, in order that I fear and do so and sin, so that they should have this for a scandal in order to reproach me.
Remember, my Elokim, Toviyah and Sanballat according to these their deeds, and also Noadyah the prophetess and the rest of the prophets who were frightening me.
The wall was completed on the twenty-fifth of Ellul, after fifty-two days.

Now it came to pass when all our enemies heard that, all the nations around us became frightened, and they fell very low in their own eyes, and they knew that this work had been performed by our Elokim.
Even in those days, the rulers of Yehudah increasingly sent their letters to Toviyah, and Toviyah's were coming to them.
For many in Yehudah were his confederates, for he was the son-in-law of Shechanyah the son of Arah, and Yehochanan his son had married the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechyah.
They also spoke of his good qualities before me, and they divulged my words to him; Toviyah sent letters to frighten me.
Now it came to pass, when the wall had been built and I had erected the doors, that the gatekeepers, the choristers, and the Leviim were appointed.
And I put Chanani my brother and Chananyah the ruler of the castle charge over Yerushalayim, for he is indeed a truthful man, and he has feared Elokim for a long time.

And I said to them, "The gates of Yerushalayim shall not be opened until the sun becomes hot, and they [the people] shall stand until they lock the doors and hold them, and station watches among the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, each one on his watch and each one opposite his house."
Now the city was wide and large, and the people were few within it, and there were no houses built.

And Elokim put it into my heart, and I gathered the rulers and the prefects and the people to trace their lineage, and I found the book of lineage of those who had gone up at first, and I found written in it:

These are the people of the province who went up from the captivity of the exile, whom Nevuchadnezzar the king of Bavel had exiled to Bavel, and they returned to Yerushalayim and to Yehudah, each one to his city.
[Those] who came with Zerubavel, Yeshua, Nechemiah, Azaryah, Raamyah, Nahamani, Mordechai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, Baanah, the number of the important men of the people of Yisroel.
The children of Parosh were two thousand one hundred and seventy-two.
The children of Shefatyah were three hundred and seventy-two.
The children of Arah were six hundred and fifty-two.
The children of Pahath-Moav, of the children of Yeshua and Yoav, were two thousand eight hundred and eighteen.
The children of Eilam were one thousand two hundred and fifty-four.
The children of Zattu were eight hundred and forty-five.
The children of Zakkai were seven hundred and sixty.
The children of Binnui were six hundred and forty-eight.
The children of Bebai were six hundred and twenty-eight.
The children of Azgad were two thousand three hundred and twenty-two.
The children of Adonikam were six hundred and sixty seven.
The children of Bigvai were two thousand and sixty-seven.
The children of Adin were six hundred and fifty-five.
The children of Ater, of Chizkiyah were ninety-eight.
The children of Hashum were three hundred and twenty-eight.
The children of Bezai were three hundred and twenty-four.
The children of Harif were one hundred and twelve.
The children of Givon were ninety-five.
The people of Beis Lechem and Netofah were one hundred and eighty-eight.
The people of Anatot were one hundred and twenty-eight.
The people of Beis-Azmaveth were forty-two.
The people of Kiryas-Yearim, Kefirah, and Beeroth were seven hundred and forty-three.
The people of Ramah and Geva were six hundred and twenty-one.
The people of Michmas were one hundred and twenty-two.
The people of Beis El and Ai were one hundred and twenty-three.
The people of the other Nebo were fifty-two.
The children of the other Eilam were one thousand two hundred and fifty-four.
The children of Harim were three hundred and twenty.
The children of Yericho were three hundred and forty-five.
The children of Lod, Hadid, and Ono were seven hundred and twenty-one.
The children of Senaah were three thousand nine hundred and thirty.
The priests: the children of Yedayah of the house of Yeshua were nine hundred and seventy-three.
The children of Immer were one thousand and fifty-two.
The children of Pashhur were one thousand two hundred and forty-seven.
The children of Harim were one thousand and seventeen.
The Leviim: the children of Yeshua with Kadmiel of the children of Lehodyah, were seventy-four.
The singers: of the children of Asaf were one hundred and forty-eight.
The gate-keepers: the children of Shalum, the children of Ater, the children of Talmon, the children of Akkub, the children of Hatita, the children of Shobai, were one hundred and thirty-eight.
The Nethinim: the children of Ziha, the children of Hasupha, the children of Tabbaoth.
The children of Keros, the children of Sia, the children of Padon.
The children of Lebanah, the children of Hagabah, the children of Salmai.
The children of Chanan, the children of Giddel, the children of Gahar.
The children of Reayah, the children of Rezin, the children of Nekoda.
The children of Gazzam, the children of Uzza, the children of Paseah.
The children of Besai, the children of Meunim, the children of Nephishesim.
The children of Bakbuk, the children of Hakupha, the children of Harhur.
The children of Bazlith, the children of Mehida, the children of Harsha.
The children of Barkos, the children of Sisra, the children of Tamah.
The children of Netziach, the children of Hatifa.
The children of Shlomo's slaves, the children of Sotai, the children of Sophereth, the children of Prida.
The children of Yaalah, the children of Darkon, the children of Giddel.
The children of Shefatyah, the children of Hattil, the children of Pochereth Hazzebaim, the children of Ammon.
All the Nethinim and the children of Shlomo's slaves were three and hundred ninety-two.
And these were the ones who ascended from Tel-Melah, Tel-Harsha: Keruv, Addon, and Immer; but they could not tell their fathers' house and their children, if they were from Yisroel.
The children of Delayah, the children of Toviyah, the children of Nekoda were six hundred and forty-two.
And of the priests: the children of Chovayah, the children of Hakkoz, the children of Barzilai, who took [a wife] from the daughters of Barzilai the Giladis and was called by their name.
These who traced their genealogy sought their records, but they were not found, and they were disqualified from the priesthood.
And Hatirshasa said to them that they should not eat of the most holy sacrifices until a priest arises for the Urim and the Tummim.
The entire congregation together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty.
Besides their slaves and their bondwomen; these were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven, and they had two hundred and forty-five male and female singers.
Their horses were seven hundred and thirty-six; their mules were two hundred and forty-five.
[Their] camels were four hundred and thirty-five, [their] donkeys were six thousand seven hundred and twenty.
And some of the heads of the fathers' houses gave for the work. Hatirshasa gave to the treasury gold, one thousand drachmas, fifty basins, priests' tunics five hundred and thirty.
And some of the heads of the fathers' houses gave to the treasury of the work; gold, twenty thousand drachmas and silver, two thousand and two hundred manehs.
And what the remnant of the people gave was gold, twenty thousand drachmas and silver, two thousand manehs, and priests' tunics, sixty-seven.

And the priests, the Leviim, the gatekeepers, and the singers, and some of the people, and the Nethinim, and all Yisroel dwelt in their cities, and the seventh month arrived, and the Children of Yisroel were in their cities.
Now all the people gathered as one man to the square that was before the Water Gate, and they said to Ezra the scholar to bring the scroll of the Law of Moshe, which Havayah had commanded Yisroel.
And Ezra the priest brought the Law before the congregation, both men and women, and all who could hear with understanding, on the first day of the seventh month.

And he read in it before the square that was before the Water Gate from the [first] light until midday in the presence of the men and the women and those who understood, and the ears of all the people were [attentive] to the Scroll of the Law.

And Ezra the scholar stood on a wooden tower that they had made for the purpose, and there stood beside him Matisyah, and Shema, and Anayah, and Uriyah, and Chilkiyah, and Maaseyah on his right, and on his left Pedayah, Mishael, Malkijah, Hashum, Hashbadanah, Zecharyah, [and] Meshullam.
And Ezra opened the scroll before the eyes of the entire people, for he was above all the people, and when he opened it, all the people stood.

And Ezra blessed Havayah, the great Elokim, and all the people answered, "Amen, Amen," with the uplifting of their hands, and they bent their heads and prostrated themselves to Havayah on their faces to the ground.

And Yeshua, and Bani, and Sherevyah, Yamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiyah, Maaseyah, Kelita, Azaryah, Yozabad, Chanan, Pelayah, and the Leviim explained the Law to the people, and the people stood in their place.
And they read in the scroll, in the Law of Elokim, distinctly, and gave sense, and they explained the reading to them.

Then Nechemiah — he is Hatirshasa — and Ezra the priest, the scholar, and the Leviim who caused the people to understand, said to all the people, "This day is holy to Havayah your Elokim; neither mourn nor weep," for all the people were weeping when they heard the words of the Law.

And he said to them, "Go, eat fat foods and drink sweet drinks and send portions to whoever has nothing prepared, for the day is holy to our Master, and do not be sad, for the joy of Havayah is your strength."
And the Leviim quieted all the people, saying, "Hush, for the day is holy, and do not be sad."
Then all the people went to eat and to drink and to send portions and to rejoice greatly, for they understood the words that they informed them of.
And on the second day, the heads of the fathers' houses of all the people, the priests, and the Leviim, gathered to Ezra the scholar, and to understand the words of the Torah.
And they found written in the Torah that Havayah had commanded by the hand of Moshe that the Children of Yisroel dwell in booths on the festival in the seventh month.

And that they should announce and proclaim in all their cities and in Yerushalayim, saying, "Go out to the mountain and bring olive leaves and leaves of oil trees, myrtle leaves, date palm leaves, and leaves of plaited trees, to make booths, as it is written."

And the people went forth and brought [them] and made booths for themselves, each one on his roof and in their courts and in the courts of the House of Elokim, and in the square of the Water Gate, and in the square of the Gate of Efrayim.

And all the congregation of the returnees from the captivity made booths and dwelt in the booths, for they had not done so from the days of Yeshua the son of Nun until that day, and there was exceedingly great joy.
And he read in the scroll of the Law of Elokim day by day from the first day until the last day, and they made the festival seven days, and on the eighth day an assembly according to the ordinance.
And on the twenty-fourth day of this month, the Children of Yisroel gathered with fasting and with sackcloth and [with] earth upon them.
And the seed of Yisroel separated from all the foreigners, and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their forefathers.
And they rose in their place, and they read in the scroll of the Law of Havayah their Elokim a fourth of the day, and another fourth they confessed and prostrated themselves to Havayah their Elokim.
And on the step of the Leviim stood: Yeshua and Bani, Kadmiel, Shevanyah, Bunni, Sharevyah, Bani, [and] Chenani, and they cried out with a loud voice to Havayah their Elokim.

And the Leviim said, namely Yeshua, and Kadmiel, Bani, Chashavnyah, Sherevyah, Hodiyah, Shevanyah, [and] Pesachyah, "Rise, bless Havayah your Elokim from everlasting to everlasting, and they shall bless Your glorious Name, for He is exalted above every blessing and praise.

You alone are Havayah; You made the heavens, the heavens of the heavens and all their host, the earth and all that is upon it, the seas and all that is in them, and You give life to them all, and the heavenly host bow down before You.
You are Havayah Elokim, Who chose Avram, took him out of Ur of the Kasdim and made his name Avraham.

And You found his heart faithful before You, and You made the covenant with him to give the land of the Kena'anim, the Chitim, the Emorim, the Perizzim, the Yevusim, and the Girgashim, to give to his seed, and You kept Your words, for You are righteous.
And You saw the affliction of our fathers in Mitzrayim, and You heard their cry by the Yam Suf.

And You performed signs and wonders against Paroh and against all his servants and against all the people of his land, for You knew that they dealt wickedly with them, and You made for Yourself a name as of this day.
And You split the sea before them, and they passed in the midst of the sea on dry land, and their pursuers You cast into the depths, like a stone in mighty waters.
And with a pillar of cloud You led them by day, and with a pillar of fire at night to illuminate for them the way in which they should go.
And You descended upon Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven, and You gave them right ordinances and laws of truth, good statutes and commandments.
And Your holy Sabbath You made known to them, and commandments and statutes and the Law You commanded them, by the hand of Your servant Moshe.

And bread from heaven You gave them for their hunger, and You took water out of a rock for them for their thirst, and You said to them to come to inherit the land that You raised Your hand to give them.
But they and our forefathers behaved wickedly, and they stiffened their necks and did not hearken to Your commandments.

And they refused to listen, and they did not remember Your wonders that You performed with them, and they stiffened their necks, and they appointed a leader to return to their bondage because of their rebelliousness, but You are a Elokim of forgivenesses, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, with much loving-kindness, and You did not forsake them.
Although they had made themselves a molten calf, and said, 'This is your god who brought you up from Mitzrayim,' and they committed great provocations.

But You,with Your abundant mercies, did not forsake them in the desert; the pillar of cloud did not turn away from them by day to lead them on the way, neither did the pillar of fire at night to illuminate for them the way in which they should go.
And You gave Your good spirit to make them understand, and You did not withhold Your manna from their mouth, and You gave them water for their thirst.
And forty years You sustained them in the desert; they did not want. Their garments did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
And You gave them kingdoms and peoples, and You separated them into a corner, and they inherited the land of Sihon, and the land of the king of Cheshbon, and the land of Og the king of Bashan.
And You multiplied their children like the stars of the heavens, and You brought them to the Land that You had promised their forefathers, to come [and] inherit [it].

And the children came and inherited the land, and You vanquished the inhabitants of the land, the Kena'anim, before them, and You delivered them into their hands, and their kings and the peoples of the land to do to them as they wished.

And they captured fortified cities and fat soil, and they inherited houses full of all good, hewn cisterns, vineyards, and olive trees, and fruit trees in abundance, and they ate and were sated, and they became fat, and they enjoyed pleasures with Your great goodness.
And they disobeyed and rebelled against You, and they cast Your Law behind their backs, and they slew Your prophets who warned them, to bring them back to You, and they committed great provocations.

And You delivered them into the hands of their adversaries who distressed them, and at the time of their distress they cried out to You, and You heard from heaven, and according to Your abundant mercies, you gave them saviors, who saved them from the hands of their adversaries.

But when they had rest, they would revert to do evil before You, and You left them in the hands of their enemies, and they ruled over them, and they returned and cried out to You, and from heaven You heard and rescued them according to Your mercy many times.

And You warned them-to bring them back to Your Law, but they behaved wickedly and did not heed Your commandments, and they sinned against Your ordinances, which man should do and live with them, and they presented a stubborn shoulder, and they stiffened their necks and did not hearken.

But You extended [mercy] upon them for many years, and You warned them with Your spirit by the hand of Your prophets, but they did not incline their ears, and You delivered them into the hands of the peoples of the lands.
But with Your abundant mercies You did not wreak destruction upon them, and You did not forsake them, for You are a gracious and merciful El.

And now, our Elokim, the great, mighty, and awesome El, Who keeps the covenant and the loving-kindness, do not belittle all the travail that has befallen us, our kings, our princes, our priests, our prophets, our forefathers, and all Your people from the days of the kings of Ashur until this day.
And You are just with all that has come upon us, for You have dealt truly and we have dealt wickedly.
And our kings, our princes, our priests, and our forefathers did not keep Your Law and did not hearken to Your commandments and to Your warnings, which You warned them.

And they, in their kingdom and with Your abundant goodness, which You gave them, and in the wide and fat land that You placed before them, they did not serve You, and they did not repent of their evil deeds.
Behold, today we are slaves, and the land that You gave our forefathers to eat its fruit and its goodness-behold we are slaves upon it.
And it lavishes its produce upon the kings whom You have appointed over us because of our sins, and they rule over our bodies and over our cattle as they wish, and we are in great distress.
Yet, despite all this, we are making a treaty and writing, and signed thereon are our rulers, our Leviim, [and] our priests.
And signed thereon are Nechemiah Hatirshasa the son of Chachalyah, and Tzidkiyah.
Serayah, Azaryah, Yirmeyah.
Pashhur, Amaryah, Malchijah.
Hattush, Shevanyah, Malluch.
Harim, Meremoth, Ovadyah.
Daniel, Gineson, Baruch.
Meshullam, Aviyah, Mijamin.
Maazyah, Bilgai, Shemayah; these are the priests.
And the Leviim; and Yeshua the son of Azanyah, Binnui of the sons of Hanadad, Kadmiel.
And their brothers: Shevanyah, Hodiyah, Kelita, Pelayah, Chanan.
Micha, Rehob, Chashavyah.
Zaccur, Sherevyah, Shevanyah.
Hodiyah, Bani, Baninu.
The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-Moav, Eilam, Zattu, Bani.
Bunni, Azgad, Bebai.
Adoniyah, Bigvai, Adin.
Ater, Chizkiyah, Azzur.
Hodiyah, Hashum, Bezai.
Hariph, Anatot, Neibai.
Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir.
Meshezabel, Tzadok, Yadua.
Pelatyah, Chanan, Anayah.
Hoshea, Chananyah, Hashub.
Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek.
Rechum, Hashabnah, Maaseyah.
And Achiyah, Chanan, Anan.
Malluch, Harim, Baanah.

And the rest of the people, the priests, the Leviim, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nethinim, and all who separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the Law of Elokim, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, all who know enough to understand.

They held with their brethren, their noblemen, and entered the curse and the oath to follow the Law of Elokim, which was given through Moshe, the servant of Elokim, and to keep and perform all the commandments of Havayah our Master, and His ordinances and His statutes.
And that we shall not give our daughters to the peoples of the land, and we shall not take their daughters for our sons.

And as for the peoples of the land who bring merchandise and all grains on the Sabbath day to sell — we shall not purchase from them on the Sabbath or on holy days, and we shall abandon [the land] during the seventh year [and] the loan given by every hand.
And we set upon ourselves the commandments to give a third of a shekel a year for the service of the Temple of our Elokim.

For the bread of the arrangement and the daily meal offering and for the daily burnt offering, the Sabbaths, the New Moons, the appointed seasons, and for the holy offerings and for the sin offerings to atone for Yisroel, and all the work of the Temple of our Elokim.

And we cast lots for the wood offering, the priests, the Leviim, and the people, to bring to the Temple of our Elokim, to the House of our forefathers at set times, year by year, to burn on the altar of Havayah our Elokim as is written in the Torah.
And to bring the first-fruits of our soil and the first of every fruit of every tree, year by year, to the Temple of Havayah.

And the firstborn of our sons and of our animals, as is written in the Torah, and the firstborn of our cattle and our flocks to bring to the Temple of our Elokim, to the priests who minister in the Temple of our Elokim.

And the first of our dough and our heave offerings and the fruit of every tree, wine, and oil, we shall bring to the priests, to the chambers of the Temple of our Elokim, and the tithe of our soil to the Leviim, and they, the Leviim, who receive tithes in all the cities of our work.

And the priest, the son of Aharon, shall be with the Leviim at the Leviim' tithing and the Leviim shall bring up the tithe of the tithe to the Temple of our Elokim, to the chambers, to the storehouse.

For the Children of Yisroel and the children of the Leviim shall bring the heave-offering of corn, wine, and oil, to the chambers where the Temple vessels and the ministering priests are, and the gatekeepers, and the singers, and we will not forsake the Temple of our Elokim."
And the rulers of the people dwelt in Yerushalayim, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one of ten to dwell in Yerushalayim the holy city, and nine parts in [other] cities.
And the people blessed all the persons who volunteered to dwell in Yerushalayim.

And these are the heads of the province who dwelt in Yerushalayim, and in the cities of Yehudah they dwelt each one in his inheritance in their cities: Yisroelim, the priests, the Leviim, the Nethinim, and the children of Shlomo's slaves.

And in Yerushalayim there dwelt of the children of Yehudah and of the children of Binyamin; of the children of Yehudah; Asayah the son of Uziyah, the son of Zecharyah, the son of Amaryah, the son of Shefatyah, the son of Mahalalel, of the children of Peretz.
And Maaseyah the son of Baruch, the son of Kol-Hozeh, the son of Chazayah, the son of Adayah, the son of Yoiarib, the son of Zecharyah, the son of the Shiloni.
All the children of Peretz who dwelt in Yerushalayim were four hundred and sixty-eight valiant men.
And these are the children of Binyamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Yoed, the son of Pedayah, the son of Kolayah, the son of Maaseyah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Yeshayah.
And after him was Gabbai Sallai, [and with him] nine hundred and twenty-eight.
And Yoel the son of Zichri was the official over them, and Yehudah the son of Hassenuah was the second in command over the city.
Of the priests were Yedayah the son of Yoiarib, [and] Yachin.
Serayah the son of Chilkiyah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Tzadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub was the official over the Temple of Elokim.

And their brethren who performed the work of the Temple were eight hundred and twenty-two, and Adayah the son of Yerocham, the son of Pelalyah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zecharyah, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malkiyah.
And his brethren, rulers over the fathers' houses, were two hundred and forty-two, including Amashesai the son of Azarel, the son of Ahzai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer.
And their brethren, valiant men, were a hundred and twenty-eight, and the official over them was Zabdiel the son of the great.
And of the Leviim: Shemayah the son of Hashub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Chashavyah, the son of Bunni.
And Shabbethai and Yazavad were over the outside work of the Temple of Elokim, of the heads of the Leviim.

And Matanyah the son of Micha, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaf was the head to begin the thanksgiving in prayer, and Bakbukyah, the second-in-command of his brethren, and Abda the son of Shamua, the son of Galal, the son of Yedusun.
All the Leviim in the Holy City were two hundred and eighty-four.
And the gatekeepers were Akkub, Talmon, and their brethren who guard at the gates; [they] were a hundred and seventy-two.
And the rest of Yisroel, the priests and the Leviim were in all the cities of Yehudah, each one in his inheritance.
And the Nethinim were dwelling in the Ofel, and Ziha and Gishpa were over the Nethinim.

And the official over the Leviim in Yerushalayim was Uzzi the son of Bani, the son of Chashavyah, the son of Matanyah, the son of Micha, of the sons of Asaf, the singers over the work of the Temple of Elokim.
For the command of the king was upon them and [his] trust was on the singers for the daily requirements.
And Pesachyah the son of Meshezabel, of the sons of Zerah, the son of Yehudah was at the king's hand for every matter of the people.
And as for the villages with their fields, some of the children of Yehudah dwelt in Kiryas-Arba and its villages, and in Dibon and in its villages, and in Yekabzeel and its villages.
And in Yeshua, and in Moladah, and in Beis-Pelet.
And in Hazar-Shual, and in Beer-sheba and its villages.
And in Tziklag, and in Mechonah and in its villages.
And in En-Rimmon, and in Zorah, and in Yannuth.
Zanoah, Adulam, and their villages, Lachish and its fields, Azekah and its villages; and they encamped from Beer-sheba until the Valley of Hinnom.
And the children of Binyamin were from Geva, Michmas, and Aijah, and Beis El and its villages.
Anatot, Nob, Chananyah.
Hazzor, Ramah, Gittaim.
Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat.
Lod and Ono, the Valley of Harashim.
And from the Leviim there were divisions to Yehudah and to Binyamin.
Now these are the priests and the Leviim who went up with Zerubavel the son of Shealtiel and Yeshua; Serayah, Yirmeyah, Ezra.
Amaryah, Malluch, Hattush.
Shechanyah, Rechum, Meremoth.
Iddo, Ginnethoi, Aviyah.
Mijamin, Maadyah, Bilgah.
Shemayah and Yoiarib, Yedayah.
Sallu, Amok, Chilkiyah, Yedayah. These are the leaders of the priests and their brethren in the days of Yeshua.
And the Leviim were: Yeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherevyah, Yehudah, Matanyah over the huyedoth, he and his brethren.
And Bakbukyah and Unni, their brethren, were opposite them in the watches.
Now Yeshua begot Yoyakim, and Yoyakim begot Eliashib, and Eliashib begot Yoyada.
And Yoyada begot Yonasan, and Yonasan begot Yadua.
And in the days of Yoyakim, the priests, the heads of the fathers' houses, were: of Serayah was Merayah; of Yirmeyah was Chananyah.
Of Ezra was Meshullam; of Amaryah was Yehochanan.
Of Melicu was Yonasan; of Shevanyah was Yosef.
Of Harim was Adna; of Meraioth was Helkai.
Of Iddo was Zecharyah; of Gineson was Meshullam.
Of Aviyah was Zichri; of Minjamin, of Moadyah was Piltai.
Of Bilgah was Shamua; of Shemayah was Yehonasan.
Of Yoiarib was Mattenai; of Yedayah was Uzzi.
Of Sallai was Kallai; of Amok was Eiver.
Of Chilkiyah was Chashavyah; of Yedayah was Nethanel.
The Leviim in the days of Eliashib; Yoyada, and Yochanan, and Yadua were inscribed as the heads of the fathers' houses, and so were the priests in the reign of Daryavesh the Parsi.
The children of Levi, the heads of the fathers' houses, were inscribed in the book of chronicles even until the days of Yochanan the son of Eliashib.

And the heads of the Leviim were: Chashavyah, Sherevyah, and Yeshua the son of Kadmiel, and their brethren were opposite them to praise [and] to give thanks by the command of Dovid, the man of Elokim, a watch opposite a watch.
Matanyah and Bakbukyah, Ovadyah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were guards, sentries of the gates [in their] watch at the thresholds of the gates.
These were in the days of Yoyakim the son of Yeshua, the son of Yehotzadak and in the days of Nechemiah the governor and Ezra the priest, the scholar.

And in the dedication of the wall of Yerushalayim, they sought the Leviim from all their places to bring them to Yerushalayim to perform the dedication with joy, and with thanksgivings, and with song, cymbals, psalteries, and with harps.
And the sons of the singers gathered and from the plain surrounding Yerushalayim, and from the villages of the Netofasim.
And from the house of Gilgal, and from the fields of Geva and Azmaveth, for the singers built villages for themselves around Yerushalayim.
And the priests and the Leviim purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gates and the wall.
Then I brought up the princes of Yehudah upon the wall, and I placed two large thanksgiving offerings with processions to the right upon the wall to the Dung Gate.
And Hoshayah and half the princes of Yehudah walked after them.
And Azaryah, Ezra, and Meshullam.
Yehudah, and Binyamin, and Shemayah, and Yirmeyah.
And of the children of the priests with trumpets was Zecharyah the son of Yonasan, the son of Shemayah, the son of Matanyah, the son of Michayah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaf.
And his brethren: Shemayah and Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, and Yehudah; Chanani with the musical instruments of Dovid the man of Elokim; and Ezra the scholar was before them.
And by the Fountain Gate and opposite them they ascended upon the steps of the City of Dovid at the ascent to the wall above the house of Dovid and until the Water Gate eastward.
And the second thanksgiving offering, which went opposite [it], and I was after it with half the people upon the wall, above the Tower of the Furnaces, and until the broad wall.

And above the Gate of Efrayim, and until the Yeshanah Gate, and until the Fish Gate, and the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, and until the Sheep Gate, and they stood in the gate of the guard.
And the two thanksgiving offerings stood in the Temple of Elokim, and I and half the prefects with me.
And the priests, Elyakim, Maaseyah, Minjamin, Michayah, Eljoenai, Zecharyah, and Chananyah with the trumpets.
And Maaseyah, and Shemayah, and Elazar, and Uzzi, and Yehochanan, and Malchijah, and Eilam, and Ezer, and the singers made their voices heard, and Yezrachyah their overseer.

And they slaughtered great sacrifices on that day, and they rejoiced, for Elokim made them rejoice with great joy, and also the women and the children rejoiced, and the joy of Yerushalayim was heard from afar.

On that day, men were appointed over the chambers for treasuries for the heave offerings, for the first gifts, and for the tithes, to gather in them from the fields of the cities the portions prescribed by the Torah for the priests and for the Leviim, for the rejoicing of Yehudah was over the priests and over the Leviim who stood [ministering].
And they kept the charge of their Elokim and the charge of purification, and [so did] the singers and the gate sentries, according to the mandate of Dovid [to] Shlomo his son.
For in the days of Dovid and Asaf, who were the leaders of the singers of yore and [who established] songs of praise and thanksgiving to Elokim.

And all Yisroel in the days of Zerubavel and in the days of Nechemiah gave the portions of the singers and the gate sentries, the requirement of each day on its day, and they consecrated [them] for the Leviim, and the Leviim consecrated [them] for the sons of Aharon.
On that day the Book of Moshe was read in the ears of the people, and it was found written therein that an Ammoni and a Moavi may not enter the congregation of Elokim forever.
For they did not come forward to meet the Children of Yisroel with bread and water, but hired Bilam against them to curse them; but our Elokim turned the curse into a blessing.
Now it came to pass when they heard the Torah, that they separated all mixtures from Yisroel.
Now prior to this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed to the chamber of the Temple of our Elokim, was a kinsman of Toviyah.

And he had made him a large chamber, and in previous times they would put there the meal offering, the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithe of the corn, the wine, and the oil, which were ordained for the Leviim and the singers and the gate sentries, and the heave offering of the priests.
Now with all this, I was not in Yerushalayim, for in the thirty-second year of Artachshasta the king of Bavel, I came to the king, and after some days, I requested of the king.
And I came to Yerushalayim, and I pondered the evil that Eliashib had done in the matter of Toviyah, by making him a chamber in the courts of the Temple of Elokim.
And I was very distressed, and I cast all the vessels of Toviyah's house out of the chamber.
And I commanded, and they purified the chambers, and I returned there the vessels of the Temple of Elokim, the meal offerings, and the frankincense.
And I knew that the portions due the Leviim had not been given, and the Leviim and the singers who did the work fled each one to his field.
So I quarreled with the prefects, and I said, "Why has the Temple of Elokim been forsaken?" And I gathered them and stationed them in their place.
And all of Yehudah brought the tithes of the corn, and the wine, and the oil to the treasuries.

And I appointed treasurers over the treasuries: Shelemyah the priest, and Tzadok the scribe, and Pedayah of the Leviim, and next to them was Chanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Matanyah, for they were deemed trustworthy, and it was incumbent upon them to distribute to their brethren.
Remember me, my Elokim, concerning this, and do not erase my good deeds that I did in the Temple of my Elokim and with its watches.

In those days, I saw in Yehudah [people] treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing stacks [of grain] and loading them on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, and figs, and all types of loads and bringing them to Yerushalayim on the Sabbath day, and I warned them on the day they sold provisions.
And the Tzorim [who] sojourned there were bringing fish and all [types of] merchandise and selling on the Sabbath to the people of Yehudah and in Yerushalayim.
And I quarreled with the dignitaries of Yehudah, and I said to them, "What is this bad thing that you are doing-profaning the Sabbath day?
Did not your ancestors do this, and our Elokim brought upon us all this calamity, and upon this city, and you are increasing the wrath upon Yisroel by profaning the Sabbath?"

Now it came to pass when the gates of Yerushalayim cast shadows before the Sabbath, that I commanded, and the doors were closed, and I said that they should not open them until after the Sabbath, and I stationed some of my youths over the gates so that no load should enter on the Sabbath day.
So the traffickers and the vendors of all types of merchandise lodged outside Yerushalayim once and twice.
And I warned them and said to them, "Why are you lodging opposite the wall? If you repeat [this], I shall lay a hand on you." Since that time, they did not come on the Sabbath.

And I commanded the Leviim that the watchers of the walls should purify themselves and come to hallow the Sabbath day. This too remember for me, my Elokim, and have pity on me according to Your abundant loving-kindness.
Also in those days, I saw the Yehudim who had married Ashdodi, Ammoni, and Moavi women.
And half their children were speaking Ashdodi, and they did not know how to speak Hebrew, and [so it was] with the language of every people.

And I quarreled with them, and I cursed them, and I struck some of them, and I plucked out their hair, and I adjured them by Elokim, "You shall not give your daughters to their sons nor take their daughters either for your sons or for yourselves.

Did not Shlomo the king of Yisroel sin with these, although there was no king like him among the great nations, beloved by his Elokim, Who appointed him king over all Yisroel? The foreign women caused even him to sin.
Shall we then hearken to you to do all this great evil to betray our Elokim to marry foreign women?"
And [one] of the sons of Yoyada, the son of Eliashib the High Priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horoni, and I drove him away from me.
Remember them, my Elokim, that they defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Leviim.
But I purified them of everything alien, and I appointed watches of the priests and of the Leviim, each one in his work.
And concerning the wood offering at appointed times and concerning the first-fruits, remember for me, my Elokim, favorably.
